articleTitle: Identification of the Most Influential Brain Waves on Impulsivity Based on a Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Impulsivity is a behavior inherent in every human being. It plays a role in the decision-making process regarding life's problems. The level of impulsivity in a person must be within reasonable limits and not excessive. It is necessary to classify the level of impulsivity to determine how high or low a person's impulsivity is. The classification is divided into five levels: Not, Less, Moderately, Active, and Strongly Impulsive, respectively. The method used for this classification is the Support Vector Machine (SVM). The SVM was chosen because it is effective for multiclass classification. The classification process is conducted using four types of feature extraction. The best accuracy results, at 98% with only two misclassifications, were obtained using feature extraction with Beta l, Beta2, and Gamma brain waves.

articleTitle: Enhancing Stacking Model Fusion for Heart Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Heart disease is responsible for about one-third of deaths in the world. Early diagnosis of heart disease is crucial to increase the chances of successful treatment and care of patients. In recent years, machine learning has shown great potential in aiding the diagnosis of heart disease. One promising machine learning approach is stacking model fusion, which combines multiple classification models to produce more accurate predictions. This study aims to analyze the effect of feature selection on the performance of stacking model fusion in predicting heart disease. The feature selection used in this study is FCBF (Fast Correlation-Based Feature Selection). The stacking model used consists of Random Forest, Linear Regression, Multilayer Perception, Extra Trees Classifier and Catboost classification algorithms as a base learner with Linear Regression as a meta learner. The dataset used in this study comes from Kaggle BRFSS focus in 2015. The results showed that FCBF feature selection can improve the performance of stacking fusion models to predict heart disease. The stacking model with FCBF feature selection achieved a prediction accuracy of 90.46%.

articleTitle: A Study on the Influence of Technology in Integrated Reporting on Corporate Financial Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: The present analysis investigates the effects of integrated reporting facilitated by technology on financial performance during the period 2013 to 2024. By merging financial and non-financial data, IR provides a comprehensive view of an organization's strategy, governance, performance, and outlook. Data sourced from Google Scholar, Scopus, and ResearchGate were analyzed using Publish or Perish and VOSviewer. Findings indicate that integrating Internet-based technologies into IR enhances resource allocation, risk management, and strategic planning, leading to improved financial outcomes. The study identifies varied correlations between IR components and financial performance, such as positive impacts on earnings per share and reduced debt costs. Despite the current low IR disclosure quality, enhancements could significantly boost company performance. This research highlights the strategic importance of technology in IR, offering stakeholders a holistic view of organizational performance and value creation.

articleTitle: Integrating Counting and Memory Challenges in Educational Games: The Development of Count and Remember
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Educational games have become increasingly prevalent as practical tools to engage students and enhance their learning experiences. The previous study demonstrates the effectiveness of games in strengthening children's cognitive skills. However, there are no further studies regarding games that simultaneously improve counting skills and memory retention. This research addresses this gap by developing a game that integrates these two cognitive domains. “Count and Remember” is a game that provides a comprehensive educational tool designed to aid in developing mathematical and cognitive skills in young learners by combining counting exercises with memory challenges. The game features interactive counting tasks, memory games, a child-friendly interface, progress tracking, and a rewards system. This study employs instructional and user-centered game design principles involving iterative prototyping and student feedback. Initial usability testing indicates that the game is both engaging and educationally effective. The findings suggest that “Count and Remember” is well received by children and considered attractive, fun, and challenging.

articleTitle: Interactive Design of Smart Screen Mirroring for Multimedia Projector Using Combined JDK and Rasberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Multimedia projector has been beneficial in enhancing the learning system. New innovations are conducted to improve the reliability and easiness of utilizing the multimedia projector. However, the utilization of VGA (Video Graphics Array) cable in multimedia projector comes with some significant limitations that contribute to their eventual obsolescence. As a multimedia projector can support the learning skills for both teacher and students, the limitation of space especially in the device localization must be under investigation. This research aims to introduce a smart mirroring device in which Java JDK and Raspberry Pi 3 is implemented for software and hardware utilization. The research has resulted an average delay of 1.75 seconds of device mirroring in which this delay time has contributed to a more practical easiness for respondents whenever presentation must be conducted. The combination of Java JDK and Raspberry Pi 3 can replace VGA cable and other devices wherever needed. For future works, a more thorough consideration must be focused on the steadiness of objects, download speed and the utilized internet provider as signals are transmitted using Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity).

articleTitle: A Microservices-Driven Digital Twin Model for Precision Farming in a Controlled Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: This paper presents a microservices-driven digital twin (DT) model for precision farming in controlled indoor environments, addressing the critical need for scalable, modular, and real-time agricultural systems. As the global demand for food rises, integrating Industry 4.0, IoT, edge, and cloud computing technologies becomes essential to improve farming process. The proposed model enhances scalability, modularity, and real-time decision making through decentralized data processing. A master-agent containerized computing architecture was employed to reduce latency and optimize environmental control. Moreover, the integration of a Kalman filter improved the accuracy of key environmental parameter adjustments. This research explored how this model can be scaled for larger farming operations and addresses challenges in system interoperability and implementation. Future work will expand this research to diverse agricultural settings, real-world validation, and ensuring data privacy and security. This study provides a framework for advancing precision farming through digital twin technology.

articleTitle: Digital Education Revolution: Analysis of ChatGPT's Influence on Student Learning in Jakarta
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: This study examines the impact of ChatGPT on student learning in Jakarta, employing the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to assess the perceptions of ease of use, usefulness, intention to use, and actual usage among university students. Using SmartPLS for data analysis, with a sample of 413 students, the study confirms significant positive relationships between perceived ease of use, usefulness, and both the intention to use and actual usage of ChatGPT. Results indicate that ease of use significantly influences students' perceptions of usefulness and their intention to use ChatGPT. Additionally, both perceived usefulness and intention to use strongly predict actual usage, highlighting ChatGPT's role as an effective educational tool in enhancing learning experiences by improving access to information and understanding of materials. The findings suggest that integrating user-friendly AI-based educational tools can significantly benefit educational practices in urban environments.

articleTitle: Utilizing Machine Learning Techniques to Analyze Primary Cilia in Postmortem Tissue Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurode-generative signified by a rapid decline in memory and cognition. Affecting millions worldwide, and without a clear solution, there is an immediate need to understand the mechanisms of the disease. Primary cilia, hair-like structures on cells that are important for cell signaling, have been implicated in AD. In this project, we aim to understand the relationship between cilia and AD. We utilize postmortem human brain tissue from AD and non-AD patients. We manually annotate the images to identify cilia and compute attributes like length, segmentation, and angle between segmented cilia. These cilia attributes are used to train 9 different binary classification machine learning models to predict if a sample is AD or non-AD. The Decision Tree, AdaBoost, and XGBoost models performed best with 88.2% accuracy and 90% F1 score. The models found that cilia segmentation and the angle between the segmentation were the most important predictors. Overall, the models can accurately classify AD vs non-AD using cilia attributes. This project may help to shed light on cilia's role in AD cellular abnormalities. Future work includes understanding cilia segmentation mechanisms and automating cilia detection so that annotation is not required.

articleTitle: Potato Leaf Disease Detection by Means of Vision Transformer and CoAtNet Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Potatoes are a food source that is beneficial for humans in various aspects, such as having nutritional and economic value. However, potato plants are susceptible to many diseases. To address this issue, various researchers have suggested methods utilizing machine learning and image processing for automatic disease type detection. This paper introduces a disease detection model for potato leaf images, employing two computer vision techniques: Vision Transformer (ViT) and CoAtNet. The dataset used in this paper consisted of 30,760 augmented images divided into seven classes. The ViT model had a test accuracy of 99.32% and a validation accuracy of99.12%. Meanwhile, the CoAtNEt model had a test accuracy of 99.58 % and a validation accuracy of 99.48 %. These results show that both models can be used in the detection of potato leaf diseases.

articleTitle: Enhancing Agricultural Water Efficiency by IoT-Based Precision Irrigation with Multiple Linear Regression Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: The increase in population has led to serious issues in water availability for agriculture, threatening global food production. Traditional irrigation methods are inefficient, resulting in significant water waste. To address this problem, our research proposes the application of the Internet of Things (IoT) to develop a precision irrigation system based on machine learning using smart irrigation valves. Environmental data and plant requirements will be processed using machine learning to provide precise solutions for water usage. The research results show a reduction in water usage by 2.6%, achieving 97.4%accuracy when comparing original data with predicted data. Additionally, the system can classify irrigation needs into three different categories based on the total volume of water applied.

articleTitle: Software Interference Prevention and SWaP-C Minimization in Cyber-Physical Systems Using Hypervisor Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Currently, hypervisor technology is an emerging topic of research. Virtualization technology, especially hypervisors and virtual machines (VM), has been widely studied but is still little applied in the cyber-physical systems (CPS) field. A hypervisor, or VM monitor (VMM), is a software program used to run multiple VMs on a single physical machine through space and time partitioning in a real-time operating system. This paper discusses the hypervisor technology to prevent software interference and to minimize size, weight, and power-cost (SWaP-C) in cyber physical systems, as well as, the application of hypervisor technology in the aerospace, automotive and control fields. By partitioning, a hypervisor can increase software safety because application programs with different criticality levels do not affect each other in failure when run in partitioned VMs.

articleTitle: Graph-Based Prompt Injection Attacks Against Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: As Large language models (LLMs) become widely used, injection attacks that induce violent or discriminatory responses from these models are also becoming more frequent. Initially, many attacks used elaborately designed textual prompts, but recently, with the introduction of models that support multi-modality, many attacks using images in addition to textual prompts have been attempted. Injection attacks using only existing text or images are mostly neutralized by latest safe aligned Large language models. In this paper, we present a new method of replacing sensitive words in the prompt with math expressions and performing an injection attack using a graph drawn based on them. By distributing illegal prompts across various input domains, for intrusion attacks against the latest safe aligned LLMs, our proposed approach achieves a very high success rate compared to SOTA existing injection attacks. We hope that the safety of the multimodal LLMs will be further strengthened by understanding the proposed injection attack.

articleTitle: Regenerative Braking System in E-Trike: Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Logic Control to Enhance Driving Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EV s) boast zero tailpipe emissions, directly improving air quality and lowering greenhouse gas emissions. Despite the promise of EVs for sustainable transportation, their limited range is a key challenge. Regenerative braking is a promising approach for enhancing the driving range. This research proposes a study of Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Logic (IT2FL) control to improve regenerative braking efficiency in an electric trike. Employing IT2FL control for regenerative braking recovers 35.84% of energy, translating to a 91.053 km increase in driving range. The IT2FL method achieved a range of 50 km/kWh, representing a significant 41.7% improvement. Furthermore, utilizing the Nie-Tan Method reducer within the IT2FL framework could extend the range by an additional 2.3 km, resulting in a 3 % increase in energy recovery. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of IT2FL control in enhancing regenerative braking efficiency for the electric trike.

articleTitle: Digital Marketing Strategies: Unveiling Multifaceted Influences on Tourist Destination Intentions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: The aims of this study are to examine the relationship between Social Media Engagement, Website usability, Mobile App Effectiveness, Tourist Satisfaction, and Intention to Visit. This research conducted a questionnaire distribution among 230 respondents who had experienced in using social media, website, and mobile applications that developed by Indonesian Tourism Government. This study utilized Smart PLS 4 to gain statistical results. The research found that Social Media Engagement does not affect Tourist Satisfaction, Social Media Engagement does not affect Intention to Visit, Website Usability influences Tourist Satisfaction, Website Usability does not affect Intention to Visit, Mobile App Effectiveness does not affect Tourist Satisfaction, Mobile App Effectiveness influences Intention to Visit, Tourist Satisfaction influences Intention to Visit. The limitation of this study is that only digital promotional activity that is being concerned. Further study could be investigated both digital and physical tourism promotional activities of Indonesian government.

articleTitle: Optimizing Indoor Vertical Farming with DDPG Reinforcement Learning: Enhancing Control of Nutrient Levels, Climate Conditions, and Plant Health
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: In indoor vertical farming systems, managing dynamic and complex environments poses significant challenges. Traditional control strategies often fall short in adapting to rapid changes in critical parameters such as nutrient levels, climate conditions, and plant health indicators. To address these challenges, this paper presents a novel approach for optimizing indoor vertical farming using Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), a reinforcement learning algorithm well-suited for environments with continuous action spaces. Our study focused on the control and monitoring of key parameters, including nutrient levels (pH and EC), climate conditions (temperature, humidity, light, and CO2 levels), and plant health indicators (biomass accumulation and leaf size structure). By defining a comprehensive state and action space, we simulated an indoor farming environment and trained the DDPG model to maximize crop yield and health.

articleTitle: Technology and Enviromental Analysis of Rooftop Solar Plant Supporting Net Zero Energy Building in Bank Office Building
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: The financial industry must adopt sustainable financial principles to support development through the use of innovative products or services that utilize solar power as a renewable energy source to reduce CO2 emissions in the operational processes. The planning of solar panels takes into account both technical aspects, as indicated by values such as reference yield, array yield, final yield, performance ratio, and battery capacity, and environmental aspects, which are evaluated by considering carbon balance. The reference yield parameter indicates similarities among the four configurations. The array yield parameter indicates that configuration 1 and 2 have lower values compared to configuration 3 and 4 by 45.7 kWDC. The final yield parameter for all four configuration yields similar results at 42 kW AC with a potential roof area of 269 m^{\prime}. The performance ratio parameter in configurations 2 and 3 reaches the highest value of 0.503. The provision of batteries for storing electricity from solar panels shows similarities among the four configurations, regardless of whether lead acid or lithium-ion LiFePO4 batteries are used. Configuration 3 achieves a significant reduction in CO2 emissions, with a reduction of 624.501 tons of CO2. The solar panel planning at the bank office building to support net zero energy building results in technical and environmental analyses. The configuration most suitable for the solar panel design at the bank office building is configuration 3.

articleTitle: Internet of Things Enabled Ovitrap in Dengue Management: Monitoring, Supervising, and Controlling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Dengue fever has spread to over 90 countries, affecting millions globally. However, due to unreliable reporting and detection systems in many regions, the true burden of the disease remains significantly underestimated, leaving populations vulnerable to continued outbreaks. Effective control requires a robust, real-time surveillance system to identify undetected cases, monitor virus co-circulation, prevent misdiagnosis, and track undocumented travel-all of which contribute to transmission in non-endemic regions. Additional factors like rapid urbanization, limited community involvement, and the high cost of eradication exacerbate the problem, particularly in densely populated areas. This project developed an Internet of Things (IoT)-based oviposition trap (Ovitrap) to address these challenges. The Ovitrap autonomously detects and counts Aedes mosquito eggs while monitoring environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, and CO2. Using AI and machine vision, it reports outbreaks in real-time, offering an innovative alternative to traditional, less effective larval monitoring approaches. Rigorously tested in both laboratory and community settings, the IoT -based Ovitrap has shown promising results in improving dengue surveillance and control. This technology offers a scalable, cost-effective solution to help reduce the global burden of dengue fever, making a significant contribution to public health and medical services.

articleTitle: Exploring the Landscape of Acoustic Authentication: Techniques, Performance and Security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a rapidly growing network of interconnected devices, transforming our relationship with technology. The potential of the interconnected ecosystem relies on seamless device pairing. Previously, complex pairing processes hindered adoption due to user frustration. Bluetooth pairing, a standardized method for IoT device interaction, has limitations such as manual entry, error-proneness, and user intervention. This can hinder user experience and integration in multi-device ecosystems. Acoustic pairing is a potential alternative to traditional wireless communication, using sound waves as a communication channel between devices. Unlike conventional Bluetooth or Wifi pairing, it requires minimal user interaction and no additional hardware. The study result indicates that in acoustic authentication, On-Off Keying, FSK, GMSK, OFDM, and DFSK are the most common modulation techniques, while the effective range is from proximity (several mm) to maximum limited to acoustic signal propagation. Combining different modulation techniques could be a promising approach to address both high range and high success rates for secure acoustic communication. First, GMSK modulation achieved a Bit Mismatch Metric (BMM) of 0.5%-3% over 50-70cm. Second, a novel deep learning-based modulation that embeds information onto channel-specific features. This approach achieved a Bit Error Rate (BER) of less than 1% over a 25 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area. Lastly, OFDM achieved a success rate greater than 95% over 20 - 220cm. Those results indicate that combining different modulation techniques, such as GMSK, deep learning-based modulation, and OFDM, can be a promising approach to achieving both high range and high success rates for secure acoustic communication systems. In addition, most of the reviewed studies are resilient against common attacks.

articleTitle: Intelligent System Luggage Lock Using NFC and NiMH Battery Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: One of the major problems during trips, especially by plane, is the security of our luggage. Classic locks deteriorate quickly due to their handling process on the conveyor belt and when loading and unloading them in and out of the plane. Since people travel increasingly by plane, they want to use their luggage for as long as possible, on as many flights as possible. For this reason, new solutions are being sought for the classic solutions of luggage locks. In this work submitted, we presented the design and implementation of a new concept for luggage locks based on modern electronics and mechanics elements. Thus, for this system, we use a lock that activates the zipper closing on the luggage inside so that the mechanical impact on it will be non-existent. The lock is controlled with NFC card access, which the luggage manufacturer uniquely gives. In our system, we introduced two NFC cards. To ensure increased security of access to the locks, we developed a mobile application called “SafeTravel”, which also allows the control of the lock through Bluetooth communication in case we don't have NFC cards with us. To use the application, the user must enter the unique PIN from the luggage manufacturer. Once the PIN is entered, the application switches to query mode with the lock, which allows access to the lock only after manually entering the ID of one of the two NFC cards. To power the system, we opted for NiMH (Nickel Metal Hydride) batteries, which, although they have a lower energy storage capacity compared to lithium-based batteries (LiPo, Li-ion), are on the list of batteries accepted for both carry-on luggage and checked bags by the bodies TSA (Transportation Security Administration) and FAA (Federal Aviation Administration). We have designed the power supply of these batteries to be possible both from a standard DC 5V source, such as phone chargers or USB outputs from laptops as well as from a solar panel in case access to a standard source is not possible it is possible.

articleTitle: Smart Neural Network Initialization for Speech Based Anger Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Affective computing, particularly anger recognition from speech, is crucial for social safety, using acoustic features and advanced machine learning to detect and mitigate potential violence. This paper introduces a novel network initialization method combining clustering techniques with least squares linear regression to improve neural network performance, enhancing training convergence and model generalization. The proposed method significantly outperforms classical approaches, showing a notable reduction in misdetection probability, regardless of the transfer function used. The approach demonstrates robustness across varying false alarm probabilities and signal to noise conditions.

articleTitle: Migration Service Process for Certification Authority Using Project Management Body of Knowledge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Termination of Certification Authority (CA) has an impact on the occurrence of massive and permanent migration to a new CA with the result that the migration process needs to be managed. Project management is appropriate for different activity sectors and greatly contributes to the success of software development or IT projects such as a migration service process for CA. The purpose of this study is to propose a recommendation on how to manage the CA migration process based on the Project Management Book of Knowledge 6th Edition. The methodology consists of three main steps which are input that uses case study, qualitative research, and data collection, process based on the process life cycle and knowledge areas, and output which is in the form of recommendation for a CA migration process. The result recommends a migration service process for CA using PMBOK 6th Edition consisting of the initiating phase, planning phase, execution phase, controlling and monitoring phase, and closing phase. Implementation of the recommendation on the study case was successful and 67% of respondents felt the migration process was progressing smoothly.

articleTitle: Leveraging Trustworthy AI and IIoT for Cost-Efficient Multimodal Quality Control in Metallurgic Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Ensuring consistent quality in metallurgic Additive Manufacturing (AM) processes, such as Cold Gas Spraying (CGS), is a significant challenge due to the inherent process variability in part quality. This study explores the integration of trustworthy Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) to multimodal quality control, with the goal of increasing in-situ test coverage of manufactured parts and process stability. An open-source software solution for data engineering and analysis was developed using the Design Science Research methodology. Experiments were conducted on a CGS system utilizing CuZn30, a copper-zinc alloy material, as a representative case study. The developed AI models demonstrated high efficiency in identifying quality deviations across multiple quality characteristics, including oxidation, geometric inaccuracies and porosity (F1-Score=0.998). The results suggest that the combination of IIoT-measurement components and AI is a cost-effective way to significantly improve test coverage, enabling the control of multiple quality attributes and process reliability in metallurgical AM using low-cost sensors and open-source software. This research contributes to the advancement of cost-effective quality control systems and provides a case study of how AI can be used to improve the reliability and stability of advanced industrial manufacturing processes with respect to multiple quality characteristics and data modalities, paving the way for mass customization as proposed in the Industry 4.0 vision.

articleTitle: Friedman Chi-Square Test Analysis of Carbon Steel Tensile Stress Data Using Python
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative method to evaluate data representation in materials science and engineering., utilizing actual tensile strength test results of carbon steel integrated into three-dimensional computer-aided drawing (3D CAD) simulations. Five groups of learners are tasked with manually plotting 100 specific datasets along simulated stress-strain displacement curves. The objective is to enhance understanding of material properties, particularly carbon steel, through practical exercises involving the application of the tensile strength equation. Learners compute force from stress values and determine dimensions from the simulated visual to calculate strain. In addition, this study uses the Friedman Chi-Square Test to analyze and compare the manual plotting results, supported by Python programming for further statistical evaluation. The findings offer valuable insights into comparing different manual plotting techniques, demonstrating their educational relevance for engineering students. Furthermore, this research establishes a method to assess the accuracy of learners' plotting outputs, which means that this exercise does not only facilitate learning, but also provides a basis for grading. It also emphasizes the importance of understanding various points on the stress-strain curve in decision-making during the design process. This approach contributes substantially to materials science education by alternative methodologies in data representation assessment and engineering education.

articleTitle: Enhanced Robust Low-Order Controller for Air Handling Units in HVAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Air handling units (AHUs), integral components of HVAC systems, play a crucial role in maintaining indoor air quality. However, implementing AHUs in critical environments poses challenges due to inaccurate modeling of these complex systems, load changes from external factors, and inherent system uncertainties, potentially leading to suboptimal control performance. In this paper, we adopt a robust control approach using µ-synthesis to address these uncertainties and disturbances, aiming to achieve robust stability and performance of the closed-loop system. To facilitate practical implementation, we reduce the complexity of the high-order controller resulting from the robust method by applying Hankel-norm approximation to obtain a reduced-order controller. Validation through simulation demonstrates a robust system response to exogenous disturbances, with root mean square errors of 2.6416 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> °C and energy savings of 8.16 % in average power consumption. The reduced-order controller is justified by its comparable robustness and accuracy to the high-order controller, with additional advantages in energy savings and computational load. The results demonstrate the proposed method's efficacy, showcasing its potential to significantly improve the control capabilities of HVAC systems.

articleTitle: Evaluating Water Spinach for Heavy Metal Phytoremediation in Indonesian Agricultural Soils
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: This study investigates the concentrations of heavy metals of Cadmium, Lead, Copper, Zinc and Mercury in the green leafy vegetable commonly grown in Indonesia. For this Water Spinach was grown in the soil samples collected from Cakung (East Jakarta), Bandung, Bogor (West Java), Megamendung (Puncak), and a greenhouse in BINDS School Simprug, Jakarta. After the spinach was grown, samples of both the spinach plant and soil (collected before and after cultivation) were analyzed in the laboratory using an Atomic Absorption Spectrometer (AAS). Laboratory analysis of soil samples reports the presence of heavy metals (Cd, Pb, Cu, Zn, Hg), within the safe limits set by FAO/WHO. However, analysis of Water Spinach grown in these soils reveals significant increase in the concentrations ranging for cadmium (0.51-0.58) mg/kg, lead (<8.73) mg/kg, and mercury (0.04-0.21) mg/kg. Computation of Transfer Factor (TF) shows TF> 1 for heavy metals of cadmium, mercury and to an extent for lead which displays the potential of Water Spinach as a hyperaccumulator for these heavy metals, making it a candidate for phytoremediation in contaminated environments. This study could pave the way for using Water Spinach in reclaiming agricultural soils contaminated with heavy metals, offering an eco-friendly solution for soil remediation in Indonesia and beyond.

articleTitle: Adversarially Robust Reinforcement Learning for Urban Traffic Signal Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Urban traffic congestion presents critical challenges, resulting in delays, environmental pollution, and significant economic costs. While traditional traffic control methods, such as fixed-time and adaptive systems, have been widely implemented, they often fail in unpredictable conditions, particularly when confronted with noisy or inaccurate data. This research proposes a robust reinforcement learning (RL) solution for traffic signal control using the RADIAL-DQN (Robust Adversarial Loss DQN) algorithm. Integrating adversarial training enhances the system's robustness to real-world uncertainties. Evaluations conducted using a SUMO traffic simulation show that the robust agent produced an increase of only 60.71% in queue length under a projected gradient descent (PGD) adversarial attack, outperforming standard RL agents, which experienced an 89% increase. These results demonstrate the potential of robust RL to improve both the reliability and scalability of urban traffic control systems.

articleTitle: The CoSTEM Model: A Conceptual Framework for Promoting Sustainable Commuting and Electric Vehicle Adoption in Organizations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Organizations worldwide are increasingly embracing sustainability initiatives to reduce their environmental impact, with employee commuting behavior and personal vehicle usage emerging as crucial areas of concern. This case study investigates the commuting patterns and willingness to adopt electric vehicles (EVs) among employees of the IKEA Perth store, a major furniture retailer committed to sustainability. Through a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data analysis and qualitative insights, the study explores the factors influencing sustainable transportation choices and proposes a comprehensive conceptual model to promote EV adoption. The findings reveal that while a significant portion of employees are open to transitioning to EVs, barriers such as upfront costs, range anxiety, and limited charging infrastructure hinder widespread adoption. To address these challenges, the Corporate Sustainable Transportation Enabler Model (CoSTEM) is introduced, encompassing strategies for workplace charging stations, monetary incentives, organizational fleet transition, systematic perception management, long-term comprehensive support, and continuous improvement. The proposed model aims to facilitate the adoption of EVs among employees and customers, contributing to reduced energy consumption, lowered carbon emissions, and alignment with the company's sustainability mission. By implementing the CoSTEM strategies and fostering collaborations with stakeholders, organizations can pave the way for a more sustainable future in transportation while enhancing employee well-being and environmental consciousness.

articleTitle: Improving Fetal Heart Sounds Using Deep Learning and Smart Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Fetal heart sound monitoring is essential for pre-natal care as it provides valuable insights into fetal health and development. However, noise from various sources can interfere with analysis techniques, resulting in inaccurate assessments of fetal well-being. This paper introduces a real-time smartphone-based system that enhances monitoring accuracy by employing an Long-Short- Term Memory based de noising algorithm and modulation-based signal processing. Experimental results underscore the superiority of the proposed LSTM-based archi-tecture over traditional linear de noising methods.

articleTitle: A Study on Methods, Challenges, and Future Directions of Generative Adversarial Networks in Stock Market Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have demonstrated a transformative capacity in financial modeling, particularly stock price prediction. This systematic literature review delves into the methodologies, challenges, and efficacy of GANs in this field, underscoring their ability to generate complex, high-dimensional data that traditional models struggle to process. By learning from the distribution of historical stock data, GANs can uncover intricate patterns missed by conventional approaches, offering a more nuanced understanding of market dynamics. However, their deployment is not without challenges, including training instability and the complex nature of financial data, which can lead to issues like mode collapse and non-convergence. The review aggregates insights from various studies to provide a comprehensive overview of current applications, highlight innovative methods, and outline future research directions to further harness GANs' potential in financial analytics. The ultimate aim is to illuminate how GANs could revolutionize traditional stock market analytics, transforming them into more predictive, robust tools for investors and analysts.

articleTitle: Cascaded Optimal Disturbance Rejection Control Scheme for Permanent Magnet Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: In this work, an optimal parameter tuning method for the PI controller is proposed to control speed and current loops of the surface mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) under the field-oriented control (FOC) strategy. Furthermore, to guarantee robustness of the system to parameter variations and disturbance effect, the extended state observer (ESO) is introduced in both speed and current control loops. The performance of the PI controller tuned by the proposed optimal tuning method is compared with the PI-PI and disturbance observer-based (DOB) controllers where the parameters of the PI schemes are tuned by the Ziegler-Nichols method. Different critical testing conditions (i.e., step changes of speed and load torque, step change of load during the acceleration of the motor) are studied to compare the performances of each scheme. Simulation results have shown that the DOB controller and ESO- based PI speed controller tuned by the proposed algorithm shown almost similar peformance, whereas an ESO-based PI-PI cascaded control scheme with optimal parameters had superior characteristics compared to other controllers in the study. The worst performance among the studied control schemes was shown by the conventional PI - PI cascaded control with largest speed drop and longest time to reach a steady state. All the control algorithms are implemented in MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Assessing Gamification, Student Engagement, and Perspectives on E-Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: The research examines the impact of student engagement, the application of gamification, and student perspectives on e-learning. The study model has three hypotheses and four variables. The operational variable has a total of 29 indicators. An online survey was conducted to collect primary data from 165 respondents in Greater Jakarta. Data analysis was performed using the Smart-PLS software using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Research findings show a strong and beneficial relationship between student involvement, gamification, and e-learning. However, the influence of student opinions on e-learning is not substantial. The research concludes that the E-learning business and the government encourage active student participation via online conversations and effective management methods. Improvement from the study highlights that incorporating gamification into e-learning systems may boost student engagement. It also emphasizes the value of active student engagement via online discussions and good management techniques in e-learning systems.

articleTitle: Leveraging Digital Innovation: Enhancing Tourist Intentions Through Social Media, Websites, and Mobile App Experiences
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: The aim of the study was to analyze the relationship between Social Media Engagement, Website Usability, and Mobile App Experiences concerning to E-Satisfaction and Intention to Visit. The Method involved selecting respondents who had used social media, website, and official government tourism applications in Thailand. The research found that Social Media Engagement influences E-Satisfaction, Website Usability influences Intention to Visit, Mobile App Experiences influence E-Satisfaction, Mobile App Experiences influence Intention to Visit, E-Satisfaction influences Intention to Visit. However, Social Media Engagement does not influence Intention to Visit, and Website Usability does not influence E-Satisfaction. The limitation of this study is its exclusive focus on studying interest in visiting Thailand through social media, websites, and applications, neglecting other promotional media. Further studies could explore other aspects influencing the decision-making process of prospective tourists when planning their travel.

articleTitle: Enhanced Model for Multi Criteria Green Port Inter-Terminal Scheduling Problem: Proposing Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Inter-terminal transport (ITT) plays a critical role in the efficiency and effectiveness of port operations, contributing significantly to the overall performance of global supply chains. This systematic literature review aims to consolidate and synthesize the existing body of knowledge on ITT, highlighting key themes, methodologies, and findings. The review covers various aspects of ITT, including operational strategies, logistical challenges, and environmental impacts. A comprehensive search of academic databases yielded a selection of peer-reviewed articles, which were then analyzed using quantitative techniques. Key themes emerging from literature include the integration of ITT with broader port operations and the impact of regulatory frameworks on ITT efficiency. Additionally, the review identifies gaps in current research, such as the need for more empirical studies on ITT's economic impacts and the exploration of sustainable ITT practices. This paper provides a thorough understanding of the state of ITT research, offering valuable insights for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers aiming to enhance port operations and supply chain resilience. Our contribution in this study is focused on developing model to improve artificial intelligent optimization model based on gaps in reviewing literature for technical design, aiming to identify variables for optimizing inter-terminal transport.

articleTitle: Optimal Hyperbolic Tangent Model for Outer Bypass MR Damper with Meandering Type Valve
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: This research discusses the application of the hyperbolic tangent model for an outer bypass MR damper with a meandering valve, which was developed by one of the authors. The hyperbolic tangent model consists of six parameters. In this study, parameter reduction was carried out using local and global sensitivity analysis, and a parameter identification strategy based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) was employed. The objective function is the relative error between the model's force and the force obtained from experiments with an outer bypass MR damper prototype featuring a meandering valve. The sensitivity analysis identifies an optimal hyperbolic tangent model with two sensitive parameters, while the remaining parameters are determined to be constant. The results show an improvement in accuracy, with the optimal hyperbolic tangent model reducing the error from 8.06 % to 7.1 %. This indicates that the optimal hyperbolic tangent model can be obtained by applying the sensitivity analysis method developed in this research.

articleTitle: Developing A Conceptual Model for Strategic Integration of Sustainability and Digitalization in Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Sustainability and digitalization represent two megatrends that profoundly impact companies, particularly those in manufacturing industries, shaping their competitive advantage and long-term market success. While there is a need for companies to converge both megatrends strategically, practitioners and scholars lack a comprehensive framework so far. This study grasps this urgent call by addressing the question of how sustainability and digitalization can be strategically integrated into the dual transformation of manufacturing corporations. Therefore, we adopt the Design Science Research (DSR) approach and collect data from a literature review and semi-structured interviews with expert practitioners. Grounded in a holistic understanding of sustainability, we derive a reference model for the dual transformation permeating all facets of business operations that includes the interdependence and strategic integration of sustainable digitalization and sustainability by digitalization. By leveraging this model, scholars and practitioners can navigate the complexities of dual transformation.

articleTitle: Welcome Message
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: On behalf of the organizing committee, it is my great pleasure to welcome all participants to the 5th International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering & Environment (TIME-E 2024). Hosted by the IEEE Indonesia Instrumentation and Measurement & Information Theory Joint Societies Chapter and the IEEE Indonesia Vehicle Technology & Intelligent Transportation Systems Joint Societies Chapter, the conference will be held from August 7 to 9, 2024, at Aston Kuta Hotel & Residence in Bali, Indonesia. After a half-decade hiatus since our last event in 2019, we are thrilled to continue the legacy of TIMEE in a hybrid format, following postponements due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
